correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge1\) and all R, upset inclusion R[j] subset U_a is controlled by the smallest successor when row nonempty; the flat implication fails exactly at rows whose minimum lies in \([a,b)\). The last such row determines output upset; adjacent upsets recover each last-occurrence entry. Distinct entries are forced by unique row minima, and singleton rows realize every partial injection. Canonical edge inclusion proves the least representative; forced and optional row minima produce the exact independent product of realization fibers. Standalone checker compares original direct semantics for every 66066 relations on chain sizes \(1,2,3,4\) and exact predicted fibers, returning ALL_CHECKS_OK; all-n proof is algebraic, not finite inference.

value.rationale: The natural structural question is how many algebraically distinct strict implications are presented by all \(2^{n^2}\) finite-chain relations, and how many relations realize a fixed operation. The matching normal form answers this for every finite chain size, gives a unique smallest representation, and resolves every nonuniform realization fiber; it is a full classification for a natural semantic class rather than a tiny arbitrary parameter slice or a bare known sequence.
